miniProject.title: A policy-linked safety campaign and reversible release decision
miniProject.brief: Extend `lmlab` with an offline safety campaign for its existing model family, using synthetic secrets and no external actions. Test the graders as well as the model, then defend a release or hold decision that preserves benign usefulness. Reuse the units' pinned PyTorch, Transformers and Inspect setup on CPU or your GPU without paid APIs.
steps: Freeze `safety/`'s behavior specification, threat model and release gates, carrying forward modality failures. Version an Inspect XSTest adaptation with deterministic and model-rubric scorers; test against held-out policy-linked hand labels before comparisons. Retain confusion counts, coverage and family errors; use hand decisions if calibration fails.

Adapt CS336's SimpleSafetyTests baseline/SFT protocol and XSTest with ordinary matched benign tasks. Score a pinned, template-balanced BBQ category against hand-checked metadata and option-order fixtures; retain context-separated accuracy, unknowns, invalids, bias and affected-group support. Compare related checkpoints only, preserving utility, harmful compliance and overrefusal separately.

Test a bounded synthetic-canary exposure update against an unchanged checkpoint and untrained canaries using withheld-suffix exact matching. Keep multiplicity, token exposure, prefix-assisted versus unprompted queries and failures in `registry/`; test a separate context-only secret against a known-source oracle, never real personal data.

Build a critique/revision pass with policy, generator and SFT-pair lineage; blind-review against unmodified responses, retaining rejected revisions. Plant a harmless apology/style/length grader shortcut and replay evaluator versions against independent labels; keep exposure manifests and source/family split checks excluding final attacks from selection.

Implement bounded direct, retrieved-text and target-history attacks using invented violations, with network actions disabled. Check query caps and transcript replay against hand-counted traces; retain every edit, feedback, token cost and failure. Separate development families from final families and static attempts from fresh adaptation.

Compare unchanged, individual and combined controls across seeds at matched generation and attack budgets, charging overhead. Freeze a development control-strength curve before held-out adaptive attacks; check outcomes by blind review, retaining utility, privacy, group and severe-failure slices, paired family/template uncertainty and narrow application-control claims.

Sign a version-bound release/hold record from predeclared uncertainty and coverage gates. Check staged shadow/canary replay and a planted behavioral regression against the previous complete configuration; retain verified rollback, monitoring roles and owned residual risks. Optionally append probe and recursive-oversight controls without changing behavioral gates.
deliverables: The `safety/` specification, threat model, exposure manifests, versioned Inspect adaptation and held-out grader-calibration evidence.
Item-level utility, safety, BBQ, synthetic-canary, revision and adaptive-attack ledgers with controls, uncertainty, failed attempts and restricted raw outputs.
A signed release/hold record with staged replay, rollback regression, residual-risk ownership and claim limits in `reports/`.

checks.name: Inspect Evals: XSTest reference task at pinned commit
checks.note: Pin inspect-ai 0.3.281; give changed scorers their own task version and replace hosted grading with calibrated scoring and hand adjudication.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 5 safety supplement: reduced baseline and SFT protocol
checks.note: Use bounded SimpleSafetyTests subsets and saved checkpoints; hand-score outputs. No public safety-label tests or large-model grader is required.

checks.name: XSTest safe and unsafe contrasts at pinned commit
checks.note: Keep safe and unsafe denominators separate; audit prefix matching against semantic labels and preserve selected row identities.

checks.name: BBQ data and metadata at pinned commit
checks.note: Join category and example identities; preserve context conditions, question polarities and template groups. Subset results do not establish global fairness.

rubric.pass: Your scorer fixtures and held-out hand labels validate confusion counts, parsing, coverage and BBQ metadata. Harmful assistance, refusal and benign utility remain distinct, with related-checkpoint identities verified.
rubric.strong: Your optional probe note specifies a hypothesis, source-held-out design, shortcut and causal controls, plus debate or recursive-oversight failure assumptions; none substitutes for behavioral gates.

rubric.pass: Your replay tests enforce attack budgets; matched controls preserve all attempts across seeds, uncertainty and slice harms. Independent labels expose the planted shortcut and distinguish scorer drift from model change.
rubric.strong: Fresh adaptation tests the frozen mitigation on held-out families; ablations distinguish application restrictions from learned behavior and preserve correlated failures and capability-loss alternatives.

rubric.pass: Your signed decision applies frozen safety, privacy, utility and coverage gates; a regression triggers verified complete-system rollback. Release, incident and residual-risk responsibilities are named, with restricted harmful outputs.
rubric.strong: A reviewer reproduces the hold or release from item records; every accepted gap has an owner, review date and reopening condition, and simulated rollout is never described as deployment certification.

miniProject.feedsInto: The policy, calibrated graders, attacks, privacy and group slices, release record and rollback tests feed Research-Scale Integration's identity-bound governance and the capstone's external safety evaluation, bounded safety module and skeptical-review defense.
